picks.title: Google Cloud rolls out Gemini for healthcare
picks.rationale: New launch (cross-section assignment: medicine only): Google's agentic, HIPAA-oriented Gemini platform for providers and health plans, with Northwell, HCA and Optum as US preview partners.
picks.excerpt: Google launched Gemini for healthcare, an agentic AI platform built with clinical and health-plan leaders and designed to support HIPAA compliance; US preview partners include Northwell, HCA and Optum.

picks.title: Voice changes may detect worsening heart failure weeks before other symptoms appear
picks.rationale: AHA 2026: AI voice analysis over a phone call flagged worsening heart failure weeks early and beat standard of care, a patient-facing remote-monitoring result distinct from the earlier AHA echo/PARAMOUNT items.
picks.excerpt: An AI-powered voice analysis system presented at AHA 2026 flagged worsening heart failure weeks before other symptoms and was much more accurate than the current standard of care.

picks.title: Large language models show potential in MRI protocoling
picks.rationale: New analysis: LLMs match radiologists at choosing the right MRI protocol, a concrete radiology workflow task; different study from the 10-14 prostate-MRI detection item it loosely matches.
picks.excerpt: A new analysis finds LLMs perform on par with radiologists at selecting the most appropriate MRI protocol for patients.

picks.title: Multi-sequence MRI-based radiomics model for predicting radiotherapy response in thyroid eye disease
picks.rationale: Peer-reviewed treatment-planning model: MRI radiomics predicts which thyroid eye disease patients will respond to orbital radiotherapy, a named disease and a real treatment decision.
picks.excerpt: A multi-sequence MRI radiomics model predicts which thyroid eye disease patients will respond to orbital radiotherapy, whose effect varies widely across patients — a treatment-planning use of imaging AI.

picks.title: FDA seeks input on telesurgery, autonomous robotics
picks.rationale: Regulator action: CDRH discussion paper on benefit-risk for autonomous and teleoperated robotic devices (docket FDA-2026-N-13135, comments due Jan. 5, 2027; workshop Dec. 2-3). Enrichment should confirm the autonomy framing carries an AI angle.
picks.excerpt: FDA's CDRH released a discussion paper on benefit-risk for robotic medical devices with autonomous or remote teleoperation capabilities (docket FDA-2026-N-13135, comments due Jan. 5, 2027; workshop Dec. 2-3).

dedup.note: Pool 16, no story_dedup drops, no clusters. Dropped as duplicate/running story: Doximity 190 health systems (history_match related to 10-26 Doximity/UpToDate; customer-count update, no new release, earnings-adjacent). Dropped as non-qualifying: STAT 'accurate advice can make us sicker' (opinion), MedCity 'look beyond speed' campaign (advocacy), Endpoints OpenAI head-of-health interview (interview, no new event), Quibim x Microsoft network (distribution deal; also related to 10-14 prostate MRI), OSU x Microsoft partnership (partnership PR, no concrete deployment named), Google AI for Healthcare Professionals certificate (Oct 29, stale and education-only). Not picked on ranking/verification: BMJ ChatGPT death lawsuit (body unverified, no image, possible overlap with politics liability coverage), NEJM AI AURA RCT, JAMA Netw Open AI-in-trials, npj SynSight (all gated/no og_image). MRI-protocoling history_match (10-14 prostate MRI, related) is a different study and task. FDA telesurgery is a new CDRH release, distinct from the 11-10 Endpoints ADVOCATE/FDA-meetings story. Gemini for healthcare is assigned to medicine by the cross-section brief. published_urls.json could not be exact-grepped (Read-only tools); none of the picks is a cross-section assignment conflict.
